clue.text: In valley, Ezekiel and others pray, continue

indicators.note: one thing sits in another, so the second phrase is placed inside the word for valley

blocks.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
Ezekiel and the other prophets belong to the Old Testament, abbreviated OT

explanation.surface: A prophet and his companions kneel in prayer in a quiet valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pray' here is the old polite 'please', not a call to worship, so 'pray, continue' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are polite, slightly old-fashioned invitations urging a speaker to carry on with the story.

clue.text: Sorry, charge is something applied to your phone

blocks.note: feeling sorry for oneself is feeling down
a charge is a load, as in a cargo or burden

explanation.surface: Phone shop talk: an apology that the fee is an app you must install.
explanation.definitionFit: Files and apps are transferred and installed on a mobile handset from the internet this way.

clue.text: British left occupies gutted hotel: major damage to London

indicators.note: a gutted building has its insides torn out, so the central letter of the hotel's name goes
to occupy a place is to move in and sit inside it

blocks.note: The Ritz is the famous luxury hotel in London's Piccadilly
standard abbreviation
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A British force moves into a wrecked hotel after severe bombing of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: THE RITZ has seven letters with R in the middle; gutting removes it, and BL moves into the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blitz was the German bombing campaign of 1940-41 that devastated much of the British capital.

clue.text: Act with inadequate zeal?

indicators.note: something inadequate is not in proper order, so the letters of the next word are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A half-hearted performance from someone lacking enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and within it the four letters of zeal are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To laze is to idle about, doing things without energy or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Sticky end delivered

blocks.note: a stub is the short end left of a pencil or cigarette
a baby that has been delivered has been born

explanation.surface: Reads like a sticky ending that has been handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky end' looks like one phrase, but it splits: Sticky is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticky person or problem is difficult and refuses to budge, like an obstinate mule.

clue.text: Novel and its library readers?

blocks.note: first meaning: Mary Norton's children's book about tiny people living under the floorboards
second meaning: people who take books out of a library on loan

explanation.surface: A book and the people who check it out of the library.
explanation.definitionFit: Library users take books out on loan, so they are its borrowers; the novel title is a proper name.

clue.text: Committee goes after money; it's where cuts will be made

definitions.text: it's where cuts will be made

blocks.note: bread is slang for money
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee chasing funds, with budget cuts looming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes after' places the committee word after the money word. The cuts look like spending cuts but are slices of a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf is placed on this wooden slab to be sliced, so it is where the knife cuts.

clue.text: Missing Latin lover at party, go too far

indicators.note: the word for lover is missing something, the letter that stands for Latin

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
taken as written
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A Latin lover gone from the party scene, someone overstepping the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin lover' looks like a stock phrase, but Latin is just the L to drop from LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess, pushing beyond sensible limits.

clue.text: Once liberal, now almost completely reactionary?

definitions.text: Once liberal, now almost completely reactionary

indicators.note: liberal means free and loose, so the preceding word is rearranged freely
almost all of the word is kept, its final letter being dropped
a reactionary turns back, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A political convert who moved from left to right.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: neoconservatives were famously former liberals who swung hard to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A neocon is a neoconservative, typically a one-time left-winger who became a hawkish right-winger.

clue.text: Gasp! A cunning plan!

blocks.note: first meaning: breathe with a whistling, laboured sound
second meaning: British slang for a clever scheme or trick

explanation.walkthrough: 'A cunning plan' echoes Baldrick from the British TV comedy Blackadder; the British slang word for such a scheme also means a breathy gasp.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is laboured whistling breathing; the other is British slang for a clever idea or stunt.

clue.text: Where, surprisingly, I find song with three words

indicators.note: a surprising turn rearranges expectations, and here the letters of the first word

blocks.note: taken as written
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to discover a three-word song.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the football chant 'Here we go, here we go, here we go' - three words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a famous terrace chant sung by British football fans, consisting of three words repeated.

clue.text: Film and its originators?

blocks.note: first meaning: Mel Brooks's 1967 comedy about a Broadway flop
second meaning: the people who make and finance a movie

explanation.surface: A movie and the people behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Producers finance and organise a movie, so they are the people responsible for creating it.

clue.text: Primarily: lounge, or lie lazily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each following word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss of a word for idling.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words both supply the letters and define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to sprawl or recline in a relaxed, lazy way.

clue.text: With head oddly empty, bear reflected in wood, spluttering 'Huzzah!'

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are emptied out, leaving only the even ones
a reflection shows things mirrored, so the bear's name is read backwards
the other pieces are put inside the letters of the wood word
spluttering speech comes out jumbled, so the word is mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
Winnie-the-Pooh, the bear
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pooh Bear, empty-headed, in the Hundred Acre Wood, spluttering a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: The empty-headed bear evokes Pooh, the bear of very little brain; oddly empty keeps only the even letters of head.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of excitement or celebration, though whoop-de-doo is often ironic.

clue.text: Again and again, penniless bloke arrives at square dances

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, so the letter that stands for penny is removed

blocks.note: the following piece is to be taken twice more
a chap is a bloke, a man
S, as in the abbreviation for square used in street names

explanation.surface: A broke man keeps turning up at square dances.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAP without its P is CHA; said once and then again and again gives three. The final S from square is loose: Sq is the usual abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance, so the plural names several of them.

clue.text: Play where that carpet's frayed; sofa's out of bounds

indicators.note: a frayed carpet has its threads in disorder, so these letters are disordered
the bounds of the word are its outer letters, and they are put out

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A shabby room where the carpet is worn and nobody may sit on the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after carpet and sofa reads as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To play a character on stage is to perform that role, taking it on as an actor.

clue.text: Not just any Tory leader in court

blocks.note: the definite article singles something out, unlike 'a'
William Hague led the British Conservative (Tory) Party from 1997 to 2001

explanation.surface: A particular Conservative leader appears in court.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch city hosts the International Court of Justice, so its name stands for that international tribunal.

clue.text: Italian renounced fussy puritanism, being hot under the collar

indicators.note: what is renounced is given up, so those letters are taken out of the long word
fussy suggests fiddling about, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian who gave up strict morality gets angry.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is removed from PURITANISM and the eight letters left are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hot under the collar is being angry or indignant, as protesters up in arms are.

clue.text: A Catholic grandee, severest for the most part in liturgy, say

indicators.note: most but not all of each word is used, so their final letters are lost

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
a toff is a posh, upper-class person
the most severe is the worst
in, as in fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: A stern Catholic dignitary taking a strict line in church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims two words at once; 'in' is not a container signal but means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is a formal set of prayers and rites, one example of religious devotion.

clue.text: With fleece surrounding one, being drawn down by gravity?

indicators.note: something surrounding another holds it within

blocks.note: to fleece someone is to skin them, cheat them of money
Roman numeral one
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A woolly-clad figure being pulled downhill by gravity.
explanation.walkthrough: The fleece hints at warm ski clothing, but it is a verb meaning to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier slides downhill on the snow, pulled along the slope by their own weight.

clue.text: Tenor misses opening of Götterdämmerung, a dotty little thing

indicators.note: the singer misses out a letter from his surname, so it is dropped
the opening of a word is its very start, so only its initial is meant

blocks.note: Plácido Domingo, the famous operatic tenor
opening letter of Wagner's opera

explanation.surface: A tenor fluffs the start of a Wagner opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking G out of DOMINGO leaves DOMINO.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is a small rectangular tile marked with spots, a witty sense of dotty.

clue.text: Strident Australian on radio: where to buy BBQs?

indicators.note: on the radio words are only heard, so what follows is to be judged by its sound

blocks.note: a barbecue is an outdoor cooker
a bazaar is a market, a place to shop

explanation.surface: An Australian radio host loudly asking where to buy barbecues.
explanation.walkthrough: The kookaburra is an Australian kingfisher with a raucous laughing call. The sound-alike, cooker bazaar, is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird's loud cackling cry makes it a noisy native of Australia.

clue.text: Implausible... but fine

blocks.note: first meaning: unconvincing, as of a weak excuse
second meaning: slender, delicate

explanation.walkthrough: 'but' suggests a contrast, yet the two meanings simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy excuse is unconvincing, and a fine thread is slender; one word covers both senses.

clue.text: Revealed in indiscreet circle

indicators.note: something revealed in a word was inside it all along, so look within the next word

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A careless secret exposed in a tight social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a flat round shape, so it is a circle in solid form.

clue.text: Man's environment is as part of Earth; is running out of time

indicators.note: time is abbreviated T, and out of means it leaves the planet's name
running suggests something flowing and shifting, so all the letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mankind's habitat as a fragile piece of the planet, with time running out.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, not humanity. EARTH loses its T, and with the two IS words the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of water between Great Britain and Ireland, so those waters surround it.

clue.text: Tucking into Bavarian lager, a couple of Germans become louder

indicators.note: food being tucked into goes inside, so the Germans go into the lager

blocks.note: Bier is German for beer
G is the abbreviation for German, twice

explanation.surface: Two Germans drinking Bavarian beer get noisier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' is a link here; the definition is the single comparative word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigger noise or sound is a louder one, greater in volume.

clue.text: Romance involving Friends character, most obscene

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the character's name goes inside

blocks.note: a gest is a medieval verse romance or tale of adventure
Ross Geller is one of the six in the TV sitcom Friends

explanation.surface: A love affair with a sitcom character turns crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Romance here is not a love affair but an old tale: GEST holds ROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means coarse or indecent, and the superlative is the most vulgar or offensive.

clue.text: Tone's set by these two chapters on self-destruction

indicators.note: destruction breaks something apart, so the letters of the word are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter, twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: A book where two chapters on self-harm set the mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Tone is musical pitch, not mood: a C clef on the staff fixes where middle C sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef on a musical stave fixes the pitch of the notes written on it.
